description: Resource files: read one, create any ClassDB resource as .tres, change one, write a shader, build a TileSet, or set a Theme colour or font size. A material is a create with resourceType StandardMaterial3D, ShaderMaterial or CanvasItemMaterial. read answers with the properties the file sets, in the form modify takes, with resourceType the engine class and scriptClass the class_name of its script when it declares one, and a Theme lists its items there as "Button/colors/font_color". create and modify answer each property given under properties as the file holds it once saved, in the same form. A create or modify whose properties made the engine change others, as a Gradient given more colours than offsets gives each new point an offset of 0, names each of those under alsoChanged with what it held before and holds now. A property holding a resource takes its res:// path; a file never imported is refused with the reimport that imports it. move takes any file of the project, a script or an image as much as a resource, or a directory, and works from the files, so it needs no editor; one serving the project is brought up to it as after a move in its own FileSystem dock, its open scenes and cached resources named for the new paths and the project settings the move rewrote taken from the file. read needs no editor either: with none serving the project, a headless engine reads the file. The ops that write a resource go through the editor when one serves the project; with none, a headless engine runs the tool the editor would and the answer says so under writtenBy. That engine runs the script of the resource, where the editor runs only tool scripts, so what a script changes as the file loads or as a property is set is put back before the save, and a resource where that cannot be done is refused and the file left as it was. Operations: read: the properties a resource file sets; create (needs resourceType): a new resource of any class; modify (needs properties): set properties on an existing resource; create_shader (needs shaderType): a .gdshader file; create_tileset (needs sources): a TileSet from texture atlases; its physics, terrain and custom data layers, and each tile's collision and other values, are written with modify after it, where a custom data layer's type takes a type name such as "int"; set_theme_color (needs controlType, colorName, color): a colour in a Theme; set_theme_font_size (needs controlType, fontSizeName, size): a font size in a Theme; remove_theme_item (needs controlType): take one item, or every item of a type, out of a Theme; move (needs newPath): move or rename a file or a directory, and every path in the project naming it. With no editor an import pass then rebuilds the project's uid cache, so a reference by uid leads to the new path, uidTable says whether it ran, and writtenByImport names the .uid and .import files it gave to scripts and assets that had none. A directory's answer names each file moved.

code.description: create_shader: the shader source, written as given. The answer says whether it compiles under compiles, and names each error the engine raised compiling it under compileErrors, with its line. Default: a minimal shader of that type. Only for op create_shader.

color.description: set_theme_color: r, g and b from 0 to 1, with a optional and opaque by default, or an html code such as "#ff8000" or "#ff800080". Only for op set_theme_color.

colorName.description: set_theme_color: such as "font_color". Only for op set_theme_color.

controlType.description: Theme ops: the theme type, a Control or Window class such as "Button", or the name of a type variation, which can be any name. A name that is no such class is set as a variation and answered with a note saying so. Only for ops set_theme_color, set_theme_font_size, remove_theme_item.

fontSizeName.description: set_theme_font_size: such as "font_size". Only for op set_theme_font_size.

includeDefaults.description: read: include properties still at their default. Default false. Only for op read.

item.description: remove_theme_item: the item to take out, its kind and name as the file writes them, such as "colors/font_color" or "styles/normal". Without it, every item of controlType goes, and the type with them, its base_type among them when it is a variation of one. The answer names each one removed. Only for op remove_theme_item.

newPath.description: move: where it goes, inside the project, and for a file with the extension it has. A file goes with its .import and .uid, and a directory with everything in it. Every path naming what moved in a scene, resource, script, project.godot or other text file is rewritten in the style it was written in, res:// or relative, and so is every relative path inside a moved file. A string naming it any other way, such as the start of a path built at run time, is answered under leftAlone rather than changed, and so is a scene or resource saved as .scn or .res, which this cannot rewrite. Only for op move.

preview.description: move: answer with what would move and change, and write nothing. A move that would be refused is refused here too, with the same reason. Default false. Only for op move.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the project directory, the one holding project.godot.

properties.description: Properties to set, keyed by Godot property name. Vectors, colours and the like may be written as {"x": 1, "y": 2} or tagged {"_type": "Vector2", "x": 1, "y": 2}, which is the form a read answers with, so a value read off one node can be written straight to another. One carrying a field its type has not, such as a z for a Vector2, is refused naming it. A colour may also be given as its html code, "#ff8000" or "#ff800080". A key may also be a colon path into one of the components of a vector, a colour, a rectangle or a transform, as GDScript names them, so one axis is written alone: "position:x", "modulate:a", "region_rect:size:y"; a component the value does not have is refused, naming the ones it has. A property holding a node takes the path to it from the node being set, such as "../Player". A property holding a Resource takes the res:// path of a file, which a read answers with its class and, when its script declares one, scriptClass, or a resource built into the scene as {"_type": "CircleShape2D", "radius": 8}, its class (an engine class or a script's class_name) beside its properties. A typed list or map of resources or nodes, such as Array[Item], takes each in the same forms, a node by its path; a read answers a resource built into the scene in that form, with what it holds away from the defaults, so it too can be written to another node. script takes the res:// path of a script to attach, one with no class_name included, and is attached before the rest are set, so the properties it declares can be given beside it. Each value is read back once set, and one the engine changed or refused is refused with what it holds. An enum property takes its number or the name of a value: as the script spells it, as the inspector shows it, or for an engine enum as the class's constant, so Add or BLEND_MODE_ADD; a value past an export range, or a number no value of an enum has, is written as given and named under outsideDeclared. A key may reach into a resource built into this one: the property holding it, a slash, then one of its own, so a TileSet's first atlas source takes "sources/0/0:0/0/probability". A list of such resources is stepped into by an element's index, so "lines/1/text" is the text of the second resource in lines and the others are left as they were. A resource kept in a file of its own, or built into the scene an instance comes from, is written in that file, or replaced here by one of this file's own. The next element of a list is made by writing to it, as the inspector's Add Element makes it: physics_layer_0/collision_layer on a TileSet with no physics layer makes its first, and "sources/0/0:0/0/physics_layer_0/polygon_0/points" a tile's first collision polygon on that layer. A whole number of 2^53 or more, such as a 64-bit seed or a resource uid, is written as its digits, {"_type": "int", "value": "9007199254740993"}, the form a read answers with: a JSON number that large can arrive as a neighbour of the one sent, so sent as a number it is refused. Only for ops create, modify.

resourcePath.description: File inside the project, such as "sprites/hero.png" or "materials/steel.tres". move: a directory too. read: also a resource kept inside a scene or resource file, by the path a read answers a property holding it with, such as "res://hero.tscn::Animation_jump".

resourceType.description: create: the resource class, such as "PhysicsMaterial" or "StandardMaterial3D", or a class_name a project script declares, which the resource is made as with that script attached. Only for op create.

script.description: create: a script to attach, for custom resources. Only for op create.

size.description: set_theme_font_size: pixels, a whole number of 1 or more. Only for op set_theme_font_size.

sources.description: Atlas sources, one per texture. A wholly transparent cell gets no tile, and the answer lists those cells as leftBlank; a strip at the right or bottom that no whole tile reaches is described in notInAnyTile. The answer gives tileSize, the size cells are drawn at, which the first source sets. A path that already exists is refused, as create_tileset would replace the whole TileSet. Only for op create_tileset.

texture.description: File inside the project, such as "sprites/hero.png" or "materials/steel.tres".

name: resource_edit
title: Edit resources
